summary: Frontend testing for Bloque B (PST self-registration + admin panels). All critical flows working: PST register/login/wizard/dashboard, admin Requisitos, admin Afiliados with filter, and all 6 Settings tabs (Hero, WhatsApp, Planes, Codigos, Banco, Analytics). Wizard completed end-to-end for a newly-registered PST user through all 6 steps (datos -> ubicacion -> fotos -> requisitos -> certificaciones -> preview). 5 requisitos rendered in wizard with 2 obligatorio badges. 3 seeded planes and 2 discount codes visible in Settings tabs. Admin sidebar shows Afiliados + Requisitos items (verified visually).

minor.issue: Returns 400 when the PST account has an already-approved empresa (test@empresa.com). Wizard save fails silently. Likely intended (approved profiles are locked), but the UI should show a clear message instead of a generic 400 toast, or hide Editar perfil for aprobado state (currently only shown for borrador/rechazado which is correct - but if user hits /pst/wizard directly it errors).

issues: Console hydration warnings: <span> cannot be a child of <select>/<option>. Caused by a wrapper span with x-ve-dynamic around <option> nodes from the dev instrumentation. Not a user-facing bug but pollutes console.

action_items: Consider hiding /pst/wizard access (or showing an informative message) when empresa.estado === 'aprobado', so users don't hit generic 400 errors from PUT /api/pst/perfil.
Investigate the <span> inside <select>/<option> hydration warnings in PSTWizard (line 206-209) — likely from a dev-instrumentation wrapper; ensure production build strips it.
critical_code_review_comments: PSTWizard.jsx (480 lines) is close to the 700-line cap but acceptable; consider splitting each step into its own component if it grows.
AdminSettings.jsx (367 lines) is fine; tabs are inline which is OK for now.

AdminLayout uses localStorage.getItem('auth_token') synchronously in useEffect – during first render navItems may show admin items by default (userRole initial state = 'admin'), which is a minor security perception issue but fine because backend enforces authorization.
